framework.name: Next Generation Science Standards — Science (K–HS sample)
framework.subject: SCIENCE
framework.description: NGSS coverage pack: Kindergarten–Grade 8 plus High School physical, life, Earth, and engineering samples.

children.title: Pushes and pulls
children.summary: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or directions of pushes and pulls.

objectives.statement: Students compare effects of push/pull strength or direction.

children.title: Change speed or direction
children.summary: Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change speed or direction.

objectives.statement: Students test a design that changes motion.

children.title: What plants and animals need to survive
children.summary: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals need to survive.

objectives.statement: Students list needs of plants and animals from observations.

children.title: Weather patterns
children.summary: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.

objectives.statement: Students record weather and describe a pattern.

children.title: Needs and where organisms live
children.summary: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants/animals and the places they live.

objectives.statement: Students match organisms to habitats by needs.

children.title: Objects in darkness need light to be seen
children.titleKo: 어두운 곳의 물체는 빛이 있어야 보임
children.summary: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that objects can be seen only when illuminated.

objectives.statement: Students explain why objects need light to be seen.

children.title: Devices that use light or sound
children.summary: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve a problem of communicating over a distance.

objectives.statement: Students build a simple communication device.

children.title: How plants and animals use external parts
children.summary: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants/animals use external parts.

objectives.statement: Students design a biomimicry solution.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Design linked to organism part function.

children.title: Parents and offspring behavior
children.summary: Read texts and use media to determine patterns in behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.

objectives.statement: Students describe a parent–offspring survival pattern.

children.title: Patterns of sun, moon, and stars
children.summary: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.

objectives.statement: Students describe a predictable sky pattern.

children.title: Seasonal daylight patterns
children.summary: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.

objectives.statement: Students compare daylight across seasons.

children.title: Describe and classify materials
children.summary: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.

objectives.statement: Students classify materials by properties.

children.title: Heating or cooling can change matter
children.summary: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.

objectives.statement: Students argue reversible vs irreversible changes.

children.title: Plants need sunlight and water
children.summary: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.

objectives.statement: Students test plant needs with a controlled comparison.

children.title: Diversity of life in habitats
children.summary: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.

objectives.statement: Students compare diversity across 2 habitats.

children.title: Earth events can occur quickly or slowly
children.titleKo: 지구 사건은 빠르게 또는 느리게 일어남
children.summary: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.

objectives.statement: Students sort events by timescale.

children.title: Shapes and kinds of land and water
children.summary: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.

objectives.statement: Students build a land/water model of a local area.

children.title: Effects of balanced and unbalanced forces
children.summary: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces.

objectives.statement: Students investigate balanced vs unbalanced forces.

children.title: Patterns of motion
children.summary: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.

objectives.statement: Students predict motion from a pattern.

children.title: Life cycles of plants and animals
children.summary: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have birth, growth, reproduction, and death.

objectives.statement: Students model two life cycles with shared stages.

children.title: Inherited traits
children.summary: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents.

objectives.statement: Students analyze trait data across generations.

children.title: Adaptation
children.summary: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals may provide advantages in surviving.

objectives.statement: Students explain an adaptive advantage.

children.title: Typical weather conditions
children.summary: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.

objectives.statement: Students graph seasonal weather data.

children.title: Solutions that reduce weather hazards
children.summary: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.

objectives.statement: Students evaluate a hazard-reduction design.

children.title: Use evidence to relate speed of an object to energy
children.titleKo: 물체의 속도와 에너지 관계 증거로 설명하기
children.summary: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.

objectives.statement: Students relate greater speed to greater energy using observational evidence.
objectives.statementKo: 관찰 증거를 바탕으로 속력이 클수록 에너지가 큼을 설명한다.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Given 3 motion scenarios, student correctly ranks relative energy and cites speed evidence.
objectives.masteryCriteriaKo: 운동 상황 3개에서 상대 에너지를 순위로 매기고 속력 근거를 제시한다.

resources.title: Speed & Energy Evidence Log
resources.description: Record observations linking speed and energy (sample placeholder).

children.title: Make observations to provide evidence of energy transfer
children.summary: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.

objectives.statement: Students identify examples of energy transfer by sound, light, heat, and electric current.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Student correctly classifies 8/10 transfer examples by mechanism.

children.title: Device that converts energy
children.summary: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.

objectives.statement: Students design and refine an energy-conversion device.

children.title: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer
Ask questions about energy changes when objects collide
children.titleKo: 물체 충돌 시 에너지 변화에 대해 질문하기
children.summary: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.

objectives.statement: Students ask testable questions and predict energy changes in collision events.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Student writes 1 testable question and 1 evidence-based prediction for a collision demo.

children.title: Identify evidence from rock formations and fossils for landscape change
children.summary: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.

objectives.statement: Students use rock layer and fossil patterns as evidence of landscape change over time.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Student cites ≥2 pattern-based evidence statements supporting a landscape-change explanation.

children.title: Make observations of weathering or erosion rate
children.summary: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.

objectives.statement: Students collect observations that evidence weathering or erosion by a named agent.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Observation log cites agent + ≥2 measurable or visible effects.

children.title: Analyze maps of Earth's features
children.summary: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.

objectives.statement: Students describe one spatial pattern of Earth's features using map data.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Written claim names the pattern and cites map evidence.

children.title: Obtain information about energy and fuels from natural resources
children.summary: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and that their uses affect the environment.

objectives.statement: Students describe one fuel/energy source, its origin, and one environmental effect of use.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Info card includes source, origin, use, and environmental effect with a cited fact.

children.title: Waves of amplitude and wavelength
children.summary: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength.

objectives.statement: Students model amplitude and wavelength.

children.title: Patterns transfer information
children.summary: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.

objectives.statement: Students compare 2 information-transfer solutions.

children.title: Internal and external structures
children.summary: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.

objectives.statement: Students argue structure–function for an organism.

children.title: Animals receive information through senses
children.summary: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process it, and respond.

objectives.statement: Students model sense → process → response.

children.title: Develop a model that matter is made of particles too small to be seen
children.titleKo: 눈에 보이지 않는 입자로 물질을 모형화하기
children.summary: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.

objectives.statement: Students use a particle model to explain a phenomenon (e.g., dissolving, air).
objectives.masteryCriteria: Model + explanation cites particles for 1 phenomenon.

children.title: Make observations to identify materials based on properties
children.summary: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.

objectives.statement: Students identify a material using ≥2 measurable/observable properties.

children.title: Conservation of weight
children.summary: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling, or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.

objectives.statement: Students graph weight before/after a change.

children.title: Develop a model of ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact
children.titleKo: 지구 영역 간 상호작용 모형 만들기
children.summary: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.

objectives.statement: Students diagram an interaction between at least two Earth systems.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Diagram names ≥2 systems and one interaction.

children.title: Gravitational force
children.summary: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.

objectives.statement: Students argue direction of gravity with evidence.

children.title: Plants get materials for growth
children.summary: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.

objectives.statement: Students argue plant growth materials with evidence.

children.title: Movement of matter among organisms
children.summary: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.

objectives.statement: Students model matter cycling in an ecosystem.

children.title: Brightness of sun vs distance
children.summary: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances.

objectives.statement: Students argue brightness–distance relationship.

children.title: Daily patterns of shadows / day / night
children.summary: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and seasonal appearance of stars.

objectives.statement: Students graph shadow or day/night patterns.

children.title: Protect Earth's resources
children.summary: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect Earth's resources and environment.

objectives.statement: Students describe a community protection practice.

children.title: Develop models of atomic composition of molecules
children.summary: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.

objectives.statement: Students build/draw a model of a simple molecule’s atomic composition.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Model correctly names atoms and structure for 1 compound.

children.title: Analyze data on properties before/after chemical change
children.titleKo: 화학 변화 전후 성질 자료 분석하기
children.summary: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.

objectives.statement: Students decide if a reaction occurred using property data.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct decision + ≥2 property citations for 3 scenarios.

children.title: Particle motion and states of matter
children.summary: Develop a model that predicts and describes changes in particle motion, temperature, and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.

objectives.statement: Students model state change with particle motion.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Model links T, motion, and state.

children.title: Newton's third law
children.summary: Apply Newton's third law to design a solution to a problem involving the motion of two colliding objects.

objectives.statement: Students apply action–reaction in a design.

children.title: Change in motion depends on force and mass
children.summary: Plan an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of the forces and the mass of the object.

objectives.statement: Students plan a force/mass investigation.

children.title: Living things made of cells
children.summary: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells; either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells.

objectives.statement: Students use microscopes/models as evidence for cells.

children.title: Function of cell parts
children.summary: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways parts of cells contribute to the function.

objectives.statement: Students model cell part functions.

children.title: Environmental and genetic factors
children.summary: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.

objectives.statement: Students explain growth with both factor types.

children.title: Cycling of Earth's materials
children.summary: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth's materials and the flow of energy that drives the process.

objectives.statement: Students model rock/material cycling.

children.title: Water cycle
children.summary: Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth's systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.

objectives.statement: Students model the water cycle.

children.title: Kinetic energy depends on mass and speed
children.summary: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data to describe the relationships of kinetic energy to mass and speed.

objectives.statement: Students interpret KE vs mass/speed graphs.

children.title: Minimize or maximize thermal energy transfer
children.summary: Apply scientific principles to design, construct, and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.

objectives.statement: Students build and test an insulation/transfer device.

children.title: Energy transfer results in temperature change
children.summary: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.

objectives.statement: Students argue energy transfer from KE change.

children.title: Model of waves
children.summary: Use mathematical representations to describe a simple model for waves that includes how the amplitude of a wave is related to the energy in a wave.

objectives.statement: Students relate amplitude to energy mathematically.

children.title: Waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted
children.summary: Develop and use a model to describe that waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.

objectives.statement: Students model wave behavior with materials.

children.title: Effects of resource availability
children.summary: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on organisms and populations.

objectives.statement: Students interpret population–resource data.

children.title: Interactions among organisms
children.summary: Construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms across multiple ecosystems.

objectives.statement: Students predict interaction patterns.

children.title: Cycling of matter and energy flow
children.summary: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.

objectives.statement: Students model matter/energy flow.

children.title: Earth-sun-moon system
children.summary: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe the cyclic patterns of lunar phases, eclipses of the sun and moon, and seasons.

objectives.statement: Students model phases/seasons/eclipses.

children.title: Role of gravity in solar system
children.summary: Develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.

objectives.statement: Students model gravity-driven orbits.

children.title: Apply scientific principles to design a method to monitor human impact
children.summary: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.

objectives.statement: Students propose a monitoring method for one human impact.

children.title: Ask questions about evidence of factors that affect global temperatures
children.titleKo: 지구 기온 요인 증거에 대해 질문하기
children.summary: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.

objectives.statement: Students ask a testable question tied to temperature-rise evidence.

children.title: Uneven distribution of resources
children.summary: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth's mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.

objectives.statement: Students explain uneven resource distribution.

children.title: Natural hazards
children.summary: Analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.

objectives.statement: Students use hazard data to inform mitigation.

children.title: Rise in global temperatures
children.summary: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.

objectives.statement: Students argue human-impact pathways.

children.title: Conservation of atoms in reactions
children.summary: Develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms does not change in a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.

objectives.statement: Students model atom conservation in a reaction.

children.title: Device using thermal energy release
children.summary: Undertake a design project to construct, test, and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.

objectives.statement: Students build a chemical thermal device.

children.title: Genes influence traits
children.summary: Develop and use a model to describe why structural changes to genes (mutations) located on chromosomes may affect proteins and may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.

objectives.statement: Students model gene → protein → trait.

children.title: Structural changes to genes
children.summary: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.

objectives.statement: Students contrast asexual vs sexual genetic outcomes.

children.title: Anatomical similarities
children.summary: Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record that document the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms.

objectives.statement: Students interpret fossil-record patterns.

children.title: Fossil record
children.summary: Apply scientific ideas to construct an explanation for the anatomical similarities and differences among modern organisms and between modern and fossil organisms.

objectives.statement: Students explain anatomical relationships.

children.title: Define design problem
children.summary: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution.

objectives.statement: Students write precise criteria/constraints.

children.title: Evaluate competing design solutions
children.summary: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints.

objectives.statement: Students compare 2 designs systematically.

children.title: Periodic table predicts properties
children.summary: Use the periodic table as a model to predict the relative properties of elements based on the patterns of electrons in the outermost energy level.

objectives.statement: Students predict properties from periodic trends.

children.title: Construct explanation for chemical reactions
children.summary: Construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction based on the outermost electron states of atoms.

objectives.statement: Students explain a reaction using valence electrons.

children.title: Conservation of atoms in reactions
children.summary: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.

objectives.statement: Students balance and justify mass conservation.

children.title: Analyze data to support Newton's second law
children.summary: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among net force, mass, and acceleration.

objectives.statement: Students analyze F=ma data.

children.title: Predict gravitational and electrostatic forces
children.summary: Use mathematical representations of Newton's law of gravitation and Coulomb's law to describe and predict gravitational and electrostatic forces.

objectives.statement: Students compute/compare force magnitudes.

children.title: DNA and specialized cells
children.summary: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the structure of DNA determines the structure of proteins which carry out the essential functions of life through systems of specialized cells.

objectives.statement: Students explain DNA → protein → cell function.

children.title: Hierarchical organization of interacting systems
children.summary: Develop and use a model to illustrate the hierarchical organization of interacting systems that provide specific functions within multicellular organisms.

objectives.statement: Students model organ-system hierarchy.

children.title: Photosynthesis transforms light energy
children.summary: Use a model to illustrate how photosynthesis transforms light energy into stored chemical energy.

objectives.statement: Students model energy transformation in photosynthesis.

children.title: Factors affecting carrying capacity
children.summary: Use mathematical and/or computational representations to support explanations of factors that affect carrying capacity of ecosystems at different scales.

objectives.statement: Students analyze carrying-capacity factors.

children.title: Cycling of matter and energy flow
children.summary: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for the cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.

objectives.statement: Students explain matter/energy cycling.

children.title: Life span of the sun and nuclear fusion
children.summary: Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the sun and the role of nuclear fusion in the sun's core.

objectives.statement: Students model solar fusion and life span.

children.title: Big Bang theory and evidence
children.summary: Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra, motion of distant galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.

objectives.statement: Students explain Big Bang with ≥2 evidence types.

children.title: Feedbacks that cause Earth system changes
children.summary: Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that cause changes to other Earth systems.

objectives.statement: Students analyze a feedback example from data.

children.title: Availability of natural resources
children.summary: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity.

objectives.statement: Students explain human–resource–hazard–climate links.

children.title: Analyze a major global challenge
children.summary: Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions.

objectives.statement: Students define criteria/constraints for a global challenge.

children.title: Design a solution to a complex problem
children.summary: Design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it down into smaller, more manageable problems.

objectives.statement: Students decompose and propose a solution path.
